`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **`@cloudflare/ai-search-snippet`** はWeb Componentベースなのでフレームワーク非依存。Astroでは`<script>`タグで動的importしてDOMに追加するのが確実（React SSR内ではカスタム要素が正しくレンダリングされない）
- `chat-page-snippet`はHistory+Chat UIをフルで提供し、AI Searchの streaming response にも対応。自前実装の数百行を1つのWeb Componentで置き換えられた
- API URLは `wrangler.jsonc` の `vars.AI_SEARCH_API_URL` で設定可能。AI Searchのエンドポイントハッシュを取得したらここに設定する
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

},\n  \"javascript\": {\n    \"formatter\": {\n      \"quoteStyle\": \"double\",\n      \"semicolons\": \"always\",\n      \"trailingCommas\": \"es5\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## src/index.ts\n\nThe  account: string;\n  bucket: string;\n  object: {\n    key: string;\n    size: number;\n    eTag: string;\n  };\n  action: \"PutObject\" | \"DeleteObject\" | \"CompleteMultipartUpload\" | \"CopyObject\";\n  eventTime: string;\n}\n\nexport default {\n  async queue(batch: MessageBatch<R2EventMessage>, env: Env): Promise<void> {\n    // Only process if manifest.json was updated\n    const hasManifestUpdate = batch.messages.some(\n      (msg) => msg.body.object.key === \"manifest.json\" && msg.body.action !== \"DeleteObject\"\n    );\n    if (!hasManifestUpdate) return;\n\n    // 1. ---

**Status: DONE**

## What was implemented

A new `catalog-generator/` Cloudflare Worker that responds to R2 Event Notifications on `dbt-artifacts-modeling`. When `manifest.json` is uploaded, it reads both `manifest.json` and `catalog.json`, generates per-model Markdown documents, and writes them to the `data-catalog` R2 bucket.

## Test results

14/14 tests pass. Tests cover:
- `inferFolder`: 4 cases (multi-segment, single-segment, only 2 fqn elements, single element)
- `generateModelMarkdown`: 10 cases (heading, description, 説明なし fallback, テーブル情報 fields, tags/なし, catalog column merge with case-insensitive description lookup, catalog sort by index, manifest column fallback, リネージ upstream list, empty upstream)

## Files changed

- `/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/catalog-generator/wrangler.jsonc` — Worker config with R2 bindings
- `/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/catalog-generator/package.json`
- `/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/catalog-generator/tsconfig.json`
- `/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/catalog-generator/vitest.config.ts`
- `/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/catalog-generator/biome.json`
- `/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/catalog-generator/src/markdown.ts` — types + `inferFolder` + `generateModelMarkdown`
- `/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/catalog-generator/src/markdown.test.ts`
- `/Users/ta93abe/Developer/github.com/ta93abe/data-engineering-with-cloudflare/catalog-generator/src/index.ts` — `queue()` handler

## Self-review findings

- The `wrangler deploy --dry-run` produces a 3.17 KiB bundle (1.33 KiB gzipped), well within Worker limits.
- R2 Event Notification queue binding is not declared in `wrangler.jsonc` (intentionally — per the spec, it's configured via Cloudflare Dashboard/API). You'll need to configure the notification rule in the Dashboard to point at this Worker's queue consumer.
- The `vitest` version is `^4.1.0` (resolved to 4.1.4) — this is a major version bump from the `ingestion` Worker's `^3.0.0`, but it works cleanly in standalone mode without `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` (which isn't needed since `markdown.ts` has no Workers-runtime dependencies).

40	  columns: Record<string, DbtCatalogColumn>;

47	// ── inferFolder ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
48	
49	/**
50	 * Maps a model's fqn to a folder path.
51	 * Drops the first element (project name) and last element (model name),
52	 * then joins remaining segments with "/".
53	 * Falls back to "other" if no intermediate segments remain.
54	 *
55	 * Example: ["modeling", "marts", "datavault", "facts", "fct_visits"]
56	 *          → "marts/datavault/facts"
57	 */
58	export function inferFolder(fqn: string[]): string {
59	  // Need at least 3 elements to have any intermediate segments
60	  if (fqn.length < 3) return "other";
61	  const intermediate = fqn.slice(1, -1);
62	  if (intermediate.length === 0) return "other";
63	  return intermediate.join("/");
64	}
65	
66	// ── generateModelMarkdown ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
67	
68	/**
69	 * Generates a Markdown document for a single dbt model.
70	 *
71	 * - If catalogNode is provided, uses catalog columns (runtime type info)
72	 *   and merges descriptions from manifest columns (case-insensitive key match).
73	 * - If catalogNode is absent, falls back to manifest columns.
74	 * - Sorts catalog columns by index.
75	 * - Extracts the last segment after "." for each upstream dependency.
76	 */
77	export function generateModelMarkdown(
78	  node: DbtManifestNode,
79	  catalogNode: DbtCatalogNode | undefined
80	): string {
81	  const description = node.description.trim() || "説明なし";
82	  const tags = node.tags.length > 0 ? node.tags.join(", ") : "なし";
83	
84	  // Build lowercase -> description lookup from manifest columns
85	  const manifestDescriptions: Record<string, string> = {};
86	  for (const [key, col] of Object.entries(node.columns)) {
87	    manifestDescriptions[key.toLowerCase()] = col.description;
88	  }
89	
90	  // Build column rows
91	  let columnRows: string;
92	  if (catalogNode) {
93	    const rows = Object.values(catalogNode.columns)
94	      .sort((a, b) => a.index - b.index)
95	      .map((col) => {
96	        const desc = manifestDescriptions[col.name.toLowerCase()] ?? "";
97	        return `| ${col.name} | ${col.type} | ${desc} |`;
98	      });
99	    columnRows = rows.join("\n");
100	  } else {
101	    const rows = Object.values(node.columns).map((col) => {
102	      const type = col.data_type ?? "";
103	      return `| ${col.name} | ${type} | ${col.description} |`;
104	    });
105	    columnRows = rows.join("\n");
106	  }
107	
108	  // Build upstream list (extract last segment after ".")
109	  const upstream = node.depends_on.nodes
110	    .map((id) => {
111	      const parts = id.split(".");
112	      return parts[parts.length - 1];
113	    })
114	    .join(", ");
115	
116	  return `# ${node.name}
117	
118	## 概要
119	${description}
120	
121	## テーブル情報
122	- **データベース**: ${node.database}
123	- **スキーマ**: ${node.schema}
124	- **マテリアライゼーション**: ${node.config.materialized}
125	- **タグ**: ${tags}
126	
127	## カラム
128	
129	| カラム名 | 型 | 説明 |
130	|---------|------|------|
131	${columnRows}
132	
133	## リネージ
134	- 上流: ${upstream}
135	`;
136	}
137

1	import { generateModelMarkdown, inferFolder } from "./markdown";
2	import type { DbtManifest, DbtCatalog } from "./markdown";
3	
4	interface Env {
5	  DBT_ARTIFACTS: R2Bucket;
6	  DATA_CATALOG: R2Bucket;
7	}
8	
9	interface R2EventMessage {
10	  account: string;
11	  bucket: string;
12	  object: {
13	    key: string;
14	    size: number;
15	    eTag: string;
16	  };
17	  action: "PutObject" | "DeleteObject" | "CompleteMultipartUpload" | "CopyObject";
18	  eventTime: string;
19	}
20	
21	export default {
22	  async queue(batch: MessageBatch<R2EventMessage>, env: Env): Promise<void> {
23	    // Only process if manifest.json was updated
24	    const hasManifestUpdate = batch.messages.some(
25	      (msg) => msg.body.object.key === "manifest.json" && msg.body.action !== "DeleteObject"
26	    );
27	    if (!hasManifestUpdate) return;
28	
29	    // 1. Read manifest.json + catalog.json from source bucket
30	    const [manifestObj, catalogObj] = await Promise.all([
31	      env.DBT_ARTIFACTS.get("manifest.json"),
32	      env.DBT_ARTIFACTS.get("catalog.json"),
33	    ]);
34	
35	    if (!manifestObj) {
36	      console.error("manifest.json not found in dbt-artifacts-modeling");
37	      return;
38	    }
39	
40	    const manifest = (await manifestObj.json()) as DbtManifest;
41	    const catalog = catalogObj ? ((await catalogObj.json()) as DbtCatalog) : null;
42	
43	    // 2. Generate Markdown for each model and write to data-catalog bucket
44	    const writes: Promise<R2Object>[] = [];
45	    for (const [key, node] of Object.entries(manifest.nodes)) {
46	      if (node.resource_type !== "model") continue;
47	
48	      const md = generateModelMarkdown(node, catalog?.nodes?.[key]);
49	      const folder = inferFolder(node.fqn);
50	      const path = `models/${folder}/${node.name}.md`;
51	
52	      writes.push(
53	        env.DATA_CATALOG.put(path, md, {
54	          httpMetadata: { contentType: "text/markdown" },
55	        })
56	      );
57	    }
58	
59	    await Promise.all(writes);
60	    console.log(`Generated ${writes.length} model documents`);
61	  },
62	};
63	
```

<title></title>
<text>
### Enable event notifications via Wrangler

#### Set up Wrangler

To begin, install [npm ↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/getting-started). Then [install Wrangler, the Developer Platform CLI](/workers/wrangler/install-and-update/).

#### Enable event notifications on your R2 bucket

Log in to Wrangler with the [wrangler login command](/workers/wrangler/commands/general/#login). Then add an [event notification rule](/r2/buckets/event-notifications/#event-notification-rules) to your bucket by running the [r2 bucket notification create command](/workers/wrangler/commands/r2/#r2-bucket-notification-create).

Terminal window

```

npx wrangler r2 bucket notification create <BUCKET_NAME> --event-type <EVENT_TYPE> --queue <QUEUE_NAME>


```

To add filtering based on `prefix` or `suffix` use the `--prefix` or `--suffix` flag, respectively.

Terminal window

```

# Filter using prefix

$ npx wrangler r2 bucket notification create <BUCKET_NAME> --event-type <EVENT_TYPE> --queue <QUEUE_NAME> --prefix "<PREFIX_VALUE>"


# Filter using suffix


# Event notifications

Event notifications send messages to your [queue](/queues/) when data in your R2 bucket changes. You can consume these messages with a [consumer Worker](/queues/reference/how-queues-works/#create-a-consumer-worker) or [pull over HTTP](/queues/configuration/pull-consumers/) from outside of Cloudflare Workers.

## Get started with event notifications

### Prerequisites

Before getting started, you will need:

* An existing R2 bucket. If you do not already have an existing R2 bucket, refer to [Create buckets](/r2/buckets/create-buckets/).
* An existing queue. If you do not already have a queue, refer to [Create a queue](/queues/get-started/#2-create-a-queue).
* A [consumer Worker](/queues/reference/how-queues-works/#create-a-consumer-worker) or [HTTP pull](/queues/configuration/pull-consumers/) enabled on your Queue.

### Enable event notifications via Dashboard

1. In the Cloudflare dashboard, go to the **R2 object storage** page.  
[ Go to **Overview** ](https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/r2/overview)
2. Select the bucket you'd like to add an event notification rule to.
3. Switch to the **Settings** tab, then scroll down to the **Event notifications** card.
4. Select **Add notification** and choose the queue you'd like to receive notifications and the [type of events](/r2/buckets/event-notifications/#event-types) that will trigger them.
5. Select **Add notification**.

### Enable event notifications via Wrangler

#### Set up Wrangler

To begin, install [npm ↗](https://docs.npmjs.com/getting-started). Then [install Wrangler, the Developer Platform CLI](/workers/wrangler/install-and-update/).

#### Enable event notifications on your R2 bucket


# Filter using prefix

$ npx wrangler r2 bucket notification create <BUCKET_NAME> --event-type <EVENT_TYPE> --queue <QUEUE_NAME> --prefix "<PREFIX_VALUE>"


# Filter using suffix

$ npx wrangler r2 bucket notification create <BUCKET_NAME> --event-type <EVENT_TYPE> --queue <QUEUE_NAME> --suffix "<SUFFIX_VALUE>"


# Filter using prefix and suffix. Both the conditions will be used for filtering

$ npx wrangler r2 bucket notification create <BUCKET_NAME> --event-type <EVENT_TYPE> --queue <QUEUE_NAME> --prefix "<PREFIX_VALUE>" --suffix "<SUFFIX_VALUE>"


```

For a more complete step-by-step example, refer to the [Log and store upload events in R2 with event notifications](/r2/tutorials/upload-logs-event-notifications/) example.

## Event notification rules

Event notification rules determine the [event types](/r2/buckets/event-notifications/#event-types) that trigger notifications and optionally enable filtering based on object `prefix` and `suffix`. You can have up to 100 event notification rules per R2 bucket.

## Event types

| Event type    | Description                                                                 | Trigger actions                            |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| object-create | Triggered when new objects are created or existing objects are overwritten. | PutObjectCopyObjectCompleteMultipartUpload |
| object-delete | Triggered when an object is explicitly removed from the bucket.             | DeleteObjectLifecycleDeletion              |

## Message format

Queue consumers receive notifications as [Messages](/queues/configuration/javascript-apis/#message). The following is an example of the body of a message that a consumer Worker will receive:

```

{

  "account": "3f4b7e3dcab231cbfdaa90a6a28bd548",

  "action": "CopyObject",


</text>

<text>
# Log and store upload events in R2 with event notifications

**Last reviewed:**  almost 2 years ago 

This example provides a step-by-step guide on using [event notifications](/r2/buckets/event-notifications/) to capture and store R2 upload logs in a separate bucket.

![Push-Based R2 Event Notifications](/_astro/pushed-based-event-notification.NdMYExDK_ZD7HLg.svg) 

## 1\. Install Wrangler

To begin, refer to [Install/Update Wrangler](/workers/wrangler/install-and-update/#install-wrangler) to install Wrangler, the Cloudflare Developer Platform CLI.

## 2\. Create R2 buckets

You will need to create two R2 buckets:

* `example-upload-bucket`: When new objects are uploaded to this bucket, your [consumer Worker](/queues/get-started/#4-create-your-consumer-worker) will write logs.
* `example-log-sink-bucket`: Upload logs from `example-upload-bucket` will be written to this bucket.

To create the buckets, run the following Wrangler commands:

Terminal window

```

npx wrangler r2 bucket create example-upload-bucket

npx wrangler r2 bucket create example-log-sink-bucket


```

## 3\. Create a queue

Event notifications capture changes to data in `example-upload-bucket`. You will need to create a new queue to receive notifications:

Terminal window

```

npx wrangler queues create example-event-notification-queue


```

## 4\. Create a Worker

Before you enable event notifications for `example-upload-bucket`, you need to create a [consumer Worker](/queues/reference/how-queues-works/#create-a-consumer-worker) to receive the notifications.


## 5\. Configure your Worker

In your Worker project's \[[Wrangler configuration file](/workers/wrangler/configuration/)\](/workers/wrangler/configuration/), add a [queue consumer](/workers/wrangler/configuration/#queues) and [R2 bucket binding](/workers/wrangler/configuration/#r2-buckets). The queues consumer bindings will register your Worker as a consumer of your future event notifications and the R2 bucket bindings will allow your Worker to access your R2 bucket.

* [  wrangler.jsonc ](#tab-panel-5918)
* [  wrangler.toml ](#tab-panel-5919)

```

{

  "$schema": "./node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json",

  "name": "event-notification-writer",

  "main": "src/index.ts",

  // Set this to today's date

  "compatibility_date": "2026-03-31",

  "compatibility_flags": [

    "nodejs_compat"

  ],

  "queues": {

    "consumers": [

      {

        "queue": "example-event-notification-queue",

        "max_batch_size": 100,

        "max_batch_timeout": 5

      }

    ]

  },

  "r2_buckets": [

    {

      "binding": "LOG_SINK",

      "bucket_name": "example-log-sink-bucket"

    }

  ]

}


```

```

"$schema" = "./node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json"

name = "event-notification-writer"

main = "src/index.ts"

# Set this to today's date

compatibility_date = "2026-03-31"

compatibility_flags = [ "nodejs_compat" ]


[[queues.consumers]]

queue = "example-event-notification-queue"

max_batch_size = 100

max_batch_timeout = 5


[[r2_buckets]]

binding = "LOG_SINK"

bucket_name = "example-log-sink-bucket"


```


# Set this to today's date

compatibility_date = "2026-03-31"

compatibility_flags = [ "nodejs_compat" ]


[[queues.consumers]]

queue = "example-event-notification-queue"

max_batch_size = 100

max_batch_timeout = 5


[[r2_buckets]]

binding = "LOG_SINK"

bucket_name = "example-log-sink-bucket"


```

## 6\. Write event notification messages to R2

Add a [queue handler](/queues/configuration/javascript-apis/#consumer) to `src/index.ts` to handle writing batches of notifications to our log sink bucket (you do not need a [fetch handler](/workers/runtime-apis/handlers/fetch/)):

TypeScript

```

export interface Env {

  LOG_SINK: R2Bucket;

}


export default {

  async queue(batch, env): Promise<void> {

    const batchId = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, "-");

    const fileName = `upload-logs-${batchId}.json`;


    // Serialize the entire batch of messages to JSON

    const fileContent = new TextEncoder().encode(

      JSON.stringify(batch.messages),

    );


    // Write the batch of messages to R2

    await env.LOG_SINK.put(fileName, fileContent, {

      httpMetadata: {

        contentType: "application/json",

      },

    });

  },

} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;


```

## 7\. Deploy your Worker

To deploy your consumer Worker, run the [wrangler deploy](/workers/wrangler/commands/general/#deploy) command:

Terminal window

```

npx wrangler deploy


```

## 8\. Enable event notifications

### `r2 bucket notification create`

Create an event notification rule for an R2 bucket

* `[BUCKET]` ` string ` required  
The name of the R2 bucket to create an event notification rule for
* `--event-types` ` "object-create" | "object-delete" ` alias: --event-type required  
The type of event(s) that will emit event notifications
* `--prefix` ` string `  
The prefix that an object must match to emit event notifications (note: regular expressions not supported)
* `--suffix` ` string `  
The suffix that an object must match to emit event notifications (note: regular expressions not supported)
* `--queue` ` string ` required  
The name of the queue that will receive event notification messages
* `--jurisdiction` ` string ` alias: --J  
The jurisdiction where the bucket exists
* `--description` ` string `  
A description that can be used to identify the event notification rule after creation

<text>
# Manage event subscriptions

Learn how to:

* Create event subscriptions to receive messages from Cloudflare services.
* View existing subscriptions on your queues.
* Delete subscriptions you no longer need.

## Create subscription

Creating a subscription allows your queue to receive messages when events occur in Cloudflare services. You can specify which source and events you want to subscribe to.

### Dashboard

1. In the Cloudflare dashboard, go to the **Queues** page.  
[ Go to **Queues** ](https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/workers/queues)
2. Select the queue you want to add a subscription to.
3. Switch to the **Subscriptions** tab.
4. Select **Subscribe to events**.
5. Name your subscription, and select the desired source and events.
6. Select **Subscribe**.

### Wrangler CLI

To create a subscription using Wrangler, run the [queues subscription create command](/queues/reference/wrangler-commands/#queues-subscription-create):

Terminal window

```

npx wrangler queues subscription create <queue-name> --source <source-type> --events <event1,event2> --<source-specific-option> <value>


```

To learn more about which sources and events you can subscribe to, refer to [Events & schemas](/queues/event-subscriptions/events-schemas/).

## View existing subscriptions

You can view all subscriptions configured for a queue to see what events it is currently receiving.

### Dashboard

## 3\. Set up a CLI tool

* [ Wrangler ](#tab-panel-5752)
* [ rclone ](#tab-panel-5753)
* [ AWS CLI ](#tab-panel-5754)

[Wrangler](/r2/reference/wrangler-commands/) is the Cloudflare Workers CLI. It authenticates with your Cloudflare account directly, so no API credentials needed.

1. Install Wrangler:  
 npm  yarn  pnpm  
```  
npm i -D wrangler  
```  
```  
yarn add -D wrangler  
```  
```  
pnpm add -D wrangler  
```
2. Log in to your Cloudflare account:  
Terminal window  
```  
wrangler login  
```

[rclone](/r2/examples/rclone/) is ideal for bulk uploads, migrations, and syncing directories.

1. [Install rclone ↗](https://rclone.org/install/) (version 1.59 or later).
2. Configure a new remote:  
Terminal window  
```  
rclone config  
```
3. Create new remote by selecting `n`.
4. Name your remote `r2`
5. Select **Amazon S3 Compliant Storage Providers** as the storage type.
6. Select **Cloudflare R2** as the provider.
7. Select whether you would like to enter AWS credentials manually, or get it from the runtime environment.
8. Enter your Access Key ID and Secret Access Key when prompted.
9. Select the region to connect to (optional).
10. Provide your S3 API endpoint.

The [AWS CLI](/r2/examples/aws/aws-cli/) works with R2 by specifying a custom endpoint.

1. [Install the AWS CLI ↗](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html) for your operating system.
2. Configure your credentials:  
Terminal window  
```  
aws configure  
```
3. When prompted, enter:  
   * **AWS Access Key ID**: Your R2 Access Key ID  
   * **AWS Secret Access Key**: Your R2 Secret Access Key  
   * **Default region name**: `auto`  
   * **Default output format**: `json` (or press Enter to skip)

## 4\. Upload and download objects

(Optional) Create a test file to upload. Run this command in the directory where you plan to run the CLI commands:

Terminal window

```

echo 'Hello, R2!' > myfile.txt


```

**デプロイ済み:**
- `catalog-generator` Worker → `https://catalog-generator.ta93abe.workers.dev`
- Queue consumer: `catalog-generator-queue`
- R2 Event Notification: `dbt-artifacts-modeling` で `.json` ファイルが作成されたらキューにイベント送信

**動作フロー:**
```
dbt build → manifest.json を R2 に PUT
  → R2 Event Notification → catalog-generator-queue
    → catalog-generator Worker の queue() ハンドラ
      → manifest.json + catalog.json 読み取り
      → モデルごとに Markdown 生成
      → data-catalog バケットに PUT
```

# customers

## 概要
Customer overview data mart, offering key details for each unique customer. One row per customer.

## テーブル情報
- **データベース**: DEVELOPMENT
- **スキーマ**: PUBLIC
- **マテリアライゼーション**: table
- **タグ**: なし

## カラム

| カラム名 | 型 | 説明 |
|---------|------|------|
| CUSTOMER_ID | TEXT | The unique key of the orders mart. |
| CUSTOMER_NAME | TEXT | Customers' full name. |
| COUNT_LIFETIME_ORDERS | NUMBER | Total number of orders a customer has ever placed. |
| FIRST_ORDER_DATE | DATE |  |
| LAST_ORDER_DATE | DATE |  |
| LIFETIME_SPEND_PRETAX | NUMBER | The sum of all the pre-tax subtotals of every order a customer has placed. |
| LIFETIME_TAX_PAID | NUMBER | The sum of all the tax portion of every order a customer has placed. |
| LIFETIME_SPEND | NUMBER | The sum of all the order totals (including tax) that a customer has ever placed. |
| CUSTOMER_TYPE | TEXT | Options are 'new' or 'returning', indicating if a customer has ordered more than once or has only placed their first order to date. |

## リネージ
- 上流: stg_customers, orders

return;\n```\n\n**b) Clean up removed models (after the writes loop, before the final console.log):**\nAdd code to list existing objects in DATA_CATALOG under `models/` prefix, compare with the set of models we just wrote, and delete any that no longer exist:\n```typescript\n    // Clean up removed models\n    const currentModelPaths = new Set(\n      Object.values(manifest.nodes)\n        .filter((node) => node.resource_type === \"model\")\n        .map((node) => `models/${inferFolder(node.fqn)}/${node.name}.md`)\n    );\n\n    const existingObjects = await env.DATA_CATALOG.list({ prefix: \"models/\" });\n    const deletes: Promise<void>[] = [];\n    for (const obj of existingObjects.objects) {\n      if (!currentModelPaths.has(obj.key)) {\n        deletes.push(env.DATA_CATALOG.delete(obj.key));\n      }\n    }\n    if (deletes.length > 0) {\n      await Promise.all(deletes);\n      console.log(`Deleted ${deletes.length} stale model documents`);\n    }\n```\n\n**c) Batch R2 writes instead of unbounded Promise.all (replace the current writes loop):**\n```typescript\n    // Generate Markdown for each model and write to data-catalog bucket in batches\n    const BATCH_SIZE = 50;\n    const entries: Array<{ path: string; md: string }> = [];\n    for (const [key, node] of Object.entries(manifest.nodes)) {\n      if (node.resource_type !== \"model\") continue;\n      const md = generateModelMarkdown(node, catalog?.nodes?.[key]);\n      const folder = inferFolder(node.fqn);\n      entries.push({ path: `models/${folder}/${node.name}.md`, md });\n    }\n\n    for (let i = 0; i < entries.length; i += BATCH_SIZE) {\n      const batch = entries.slice(i, i + BATCH_SIZE);\n      await Promise.all(\n        batch.map((entry) =>\n          env.DATA_CATALOG.put(entry.path, entry.md, {\n            httpMetadata: { contentType: \"text/markdown\" },\n          })\n        )\n      );\n    }\n```\n\n## Your HTMLは正しく出力されています。`define:vars` でURLも埋め込まれている。問題は `import("@cloudflare/ai-search-snippet")` が本番環境で解決できていないことです。`define:vars` を使ったスクリプトはインラインスクリプトになるため、`import()` が使えません。

`define:vars` と動的importは共存できないので、分離します。
